title: Historical Background & Making of the Constitution

questions.q: Which one of the following was provided for by the Regulating Act of 1773?
o: A Board of Control was created to supervise the political affairs of the Company
The legislative functions of the Governor-General's council were separated from its executive functions
The Company's territories in India were transferred to the British Crown
The Governor of Bengal was designated Governor-General of Bengal, assisted by an Executive Council of four members
questions.e: The Regulating Act was Parliament's first attempt to rein in the Company, so it centralised power in Bengal under the Governor-General and a four-member council. The Board of Control came later (1784), separation of legislative and executive functions in 1853, and transfer to the Crown in 1858.
questions.h: Regulating Act = first reining-in: one Governor-General, four councillors, one Supreme Court.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Regulating Act of 1773:
1. It made the Governors of Bombay and Madras subordinate to the Governor-General of Bengal in matters of war, peace and diplomacy.
2. It established a Supreme Court at Calcutta.
3. It created a Board of Control to supervise the political affairs of the Company.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Act centralised control in Bengal and set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774). The Board of Control was a creation of Pitt's India Act of 1784, not the Regulating Act.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Act : Provision
1. Regulating Act 1773 : Supreme Court at Calcutta
2. Pitt's India Act 1784 : Board of Control
3. Charter Act 1813 : Complete end of the Company's monopoly, including tea and trade with China
4. Charter Act 1833 : Introduction of open competition for the civil service
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: The first two pairs are correct. The 1813 Act ended the Company's trade monopoly in India but left the tea and China trade monopoly with it, which went only in 1833. Open competition for the civil service came with the Charter Act of 1853.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Charter Act of 1813:
1. It ended the Company's monopoly over trade with China and in tea.
2. It provided that a sum of not less than one lakh rupees be spent annually on education in India.
3. It allowed Christian missionaries to come to India and propagate their religion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 1813 Act ended the Company's Indian trade monopoly but retained its monopoly over tea and the China trade, which went only in 1833. It added the education grant and opened India to missionaries.
questions.h: 1813: Missionaries come, money for Education, monopoly mostly goes - tea and China stay.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Charter Act of 1833 centralised legislative power in the Governor-General-in-Council.
Statement-II: The Act deprived the Presidencies of Bombay and Madras of their legislative powers.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The 1833 Act made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India. Stripping Bombay and Madras of the power to make laws is exactly how legislation was centralised in one body.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Charter Act of 1833:
1. It made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
2. It separated the legislative functions of the Governor-General's council from its executive functions.
3. It added a Law Member to the Governor-General's council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 1833 Act created the Governor-General of India and added a fourth (Law) member, Macaulay being the first. Separation of legislative and executive functions came with the Charter Act of 1853.

questions.q: The Charter Act of 1853 is notable because it
o: separated the legislative functions of the Governor-General's council from its executive functions
created the post of Law Member in the Governor-General's council
gave legal recognition to the portfolio system
questions.e: The 1853 Act provided for a separate Legislative Council (a mini-Parliament in outline) with its own additional members. The Law Member dates from 1833, separate electorates from 1909 and the portfolio system from 1861.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Charter Act of 1853?
o: It introduced open competition as the basis of recruitment to the civil service
It separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's council
It deprived the Court of Directors of the right of patronage in civil service appointments
It abolished the East India Company and transferred its rule to the Crown
questions.e: Open competition replaced the Directors' nominations, which ended their patronage. The Company itself was abolished only after the 1857 revolt, by the Government of India Act 1858.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Government of India Act 1858:
1. It abolished the East India Company and vested the powers of Government in the Crown.
2. It created the office of Secretary of State for India, a member of the British Cabinet, assisted by a council of 15 members.
3. The Viceroy was made directly responsible to the British Parliament, bypassing the Secretary of State.
4. The Governor-General of India was designated the Viceroy.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Act was the response to the revolt of 1857. The Secretary of State was answerable to Parliament and the Viceroy to the Secretary of State; the Board of Control (1784) and Court of Directors were abolished with the Company, and the Governor-General became Viceroy.

questions.q: The Queen's Proclamation of 1 November 1858, which announced the transfer of the Company's rule to the Crown, was read out at Allahabad by
questions.e: After the revolt of 1857 the Government of India Act 1858 transferred power, and Canning, as the first Viceroy, announced the Queen's promises of equal treatment and non-interference in religion. Lytton presided over the 1877 Delhi Durbar proclaiming Victoria Empress.
questions.s: Spectrum, Modern India, chapter on the Revolt of 1857 (aftermath)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Councils Act of 1861:
1. It introduced the principle of election for non-official members of the Legislative Council.
2. It gave legal recognition to the portfolio system.
3. It restored the legislative powers of the Bombay and Madras Presidencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Act marked the beginning of representative institutions through the nomination of non-official Indians, not election. It legalised Canning's portfolio system and gave back legislative powers taken away in 1833.
questions.h: 1861 = Portfolio + Presidencies restored; nomination, not election.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 expanded the functions of the legislative councils by allowing members to discuss the budget.
Statement-II: The Act empowered members to vote on the budget and to ask supplementary questions.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The 1892 Act allowed members to discuss the budget and put questions to the executive, but with no power to vote on the budget or ask supplementary questions; these further rights came in 1909.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms):
1. It introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
2. An Indian was for the first time appointed to the Viceroy's Executive Council.
3. It provided for direct election to the Imperial Legislative Council on a territorial basis.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the Law Member, and Muslims got separate electorates, which is why Minto is called the father of communal electorates. Elections remained indirect and based on classes and interests, not territory.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding the working of dyarchy under the Government of India Act 1919:
Subject : Category
1. Education : Transferred
2. Law and order : Reserved
3. Irrigation : Reserved
4. Local self-government : Transferred
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: Under dyarchy the Governor administered Reserved subjects such as law and order, finance, land revenue and irrigation with his executive council, while elected ministers handled Transferred subjects such as education, health and local self-government.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Government of India Act 1919:
1. It created the Federal Court at the Centre.
2. It introduced a bicameral legislature at the Centre with a Council of State and a Legislative Assembly.
3. It separated provincial budgets from the Central budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 1919 Act made the Central legislature bicameral and allowed provinces to present their own budgets. The Federal Court came with the Government of India Act 1935.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act 1935?
o: Introduction of dyarchy in the provinces
questions.e: The 1935 Act abolished dyarchy in the provinces (introduced in 1919) and gave provincial autonomy, while proposing dyarchy at the Centre. The Federation never came into being.

questions.q: Under the Government of India Act 1935, residuary legislative powers (subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists) were vested in
o: the Secretary of State for India
questions.e: The 1935 Act had Federal, Provincial and Concurrent lists, but left residuary powers with neither legislature: the Governor-General could allot them to either. The Constitution of India instead gives them to Parliament (Art 248).

questions.q:
Statement-I: The federal part of the Government of India Act 1935 never came into operation.
Statement-II: The Act made the Federation conditional on the accession of princely states entitled to at least half the seats allotted to the states in the federal upper house and having at least half the population of the states.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The required number of princely states never agreed to join, so the Federation, which needed them, never materialised; the provincial part alone was brought into force in 1937.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Acts in chronological order:
1. Indian Councils Act 1909
2. Government of India Act 1919
3. Government of India Act 1858
4. Indian Councils Act 1892
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
questions.e: The sequence is 1858 (Crown takes over), 1892 (limited indirect election), 1909 (Morley-Minto) and 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford).

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Charter Act 1833
2. Pitt's India Act
3. Regulating Act
4. Charter Act 1853
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
questions.e: The order is Regulating Act 1773, Pitt's India Act 1784, Charter Act 1833 and Charter Act 1853.

questions.q:
Match the following:
List-I (Act) with List-II (Feature)
A. Indian Councils Act 1892
B. Indian Councils Act 1909
C. Government of India Act 1919
D. Government of India Act 1935

1. Provincial dyarchy
2. Right of members to discuss the budget and put questions
3. Separate electorates for Muslims
4. Provincial autonomy and Federal Court
Which one of the following is the correct matching?
questions.e: Each Act's headline reform: the 1892 Act allowed budget discussion, the 1909 Act brought separate electorates, the 1919 Act introduced provincial dyarchy and the 1935 Act gave provincial autonomy and created the Federal Court.

questions.q:
Match the following:
List-I (Development) with List-II (Description)
A. Nehru Report 1928
B. Communal Award 1932
C. Poona Pact 1932
D. August Offer 1940

1. Separate electorates for the depressed classes announced by the British Prime Minister
2. Reserved seats for the depressed classes within the general electorate
3. Dominion status as the goal and a constitution-making body after the war
4. Dominion status and a statement of fundamental rights drafted by Indians
Which one of the following is the correct matching?
questions.e: The Nehru Report was India's own constitutional draft. The Communal Award gave separate electorates to the depressed classes, which Gandhi opposed by fast; the Poona Pact replaced them with reserved seats. The August Offer promised a body to frame the Constitution after the war.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Cabinet Mission 1946:
1. It rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan.
2. It proposed a Union of India with the Centre dealing only with Foreign Affairs, Defence and Communications.
3. Lord Mountbatten was a member of the Mission.
4. It proposed that the Constituent Assembly be elected by universal adult franchise.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Mission (Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps and A.V. Alexander) proposed a loose union with grouping of provinces. Mountbatten arrived as Viceroy only in 1947, and the Assembly was elected indirectly by provincial legislatures, not by universal adult franchise.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Constituent Assembly of India was not elected on the basis of universal adult franchise.
Statement-II: Its members were elected by the members of the provincial legislative assemblies, while the princely states' representatives were nominated.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because the provincial assemblies were themselves elected on a limited franchise, a body chosen by them could not be a product of adult franchise.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Independence Act 1947:
1. The British paramountcy over the princely states lapsed.
2. The Governor-General of each dominion was to be appointed by the British Government on the advice of the Secretary of State for India.
3. The Constituent Assembly of each dominion could repeal any British Act, including the Independence Act.
4. The British Crown retained the power to veto bills passed by the dominion legislatures.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Act ended paramountcy and let each Constituent Assembly repeal British Acts. The Governor-General became a constitutional head chosen on the dominion cabinet's advice, and the Crown's veto was withdrawn, since a dominion could not be independent while London could disallow its laws.

questions.q: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan the total strength of the Constituent Assembly was to be
questions.e: It was 292 members from the Governors' provinces, 4 from the Chief Commissioners' provinces and up to 93 from the princely states. After partition and the Muslim League's absence it fell to 299.

questions.q: At the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly on 9 December 1946, who was elected temporary president?
questions.e: Sinha was the oldest member, so he was the interim president. Two days later, on 11 December 1946, Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent president.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constituent Assembly:
1. Rajendra Prasad was elected its permanent president on 11 December 1946.
2. H.C. Mukherjee was elected its vice-president.
3. B.N. Rau was the Chairman of its Drafting Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser who prepared the initial draft; the Drafting Committee was chaired by Ambedkar.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Objectives Resolution:
1. It was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946.
2. It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.
3. It was moved by Rajendra Prasad.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Nehru moved it in 1946 and the Assembly adopted it on 22 January 1947. It later became the basis for the Preamble.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly:
1. It was set up on 29 August 1947.
2. It was a seven-member committee chaired by B.R. Ambedkar.
3. T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan, who died.
4. Jawaharlal Nehru was a member.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Nehru was never on the Drafting Committee. Members included Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, K.M. Munshi, Saadulla, and others replaced after a death or resignation.

questions.q:
Match the following Committees of the Constituent Assembly with their chairmen:
A. Union Constitution Committee
B. Provincial Constitution Committee
C. Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee
D. Minorities Sub-Committee

1. J.B. Kripalani
2. Jawaharlal Nehru
3. Vallabhbhai Patel
4. H.C. Mukherjee
Which one of the following is the correct matching?
questions.e: Nehru chaired the Union committees and Patel the Provincial one. The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee under Kripalani and the Minorities Sub-Committee under H.C. Mukherjee were part of Patel's Advisory Committee.

questions.q: Which of the following committees of the Constituent Assembly was NOT chaired by Rajendra Prasad?
o: Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly
Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag
questions.e: G.V. Mavalankar chaired the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly. Rajendra Prasad chaired the Rules of Procedure, Steering and Flag committees.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.
2. Members signed the Constitution on 24 January 1950.
3. The Constitution came into force in its entirety on 26 November 1949.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only a few provisions, such as those on citizenship, elections and the provisional Parliament, came into force on 26 November 1949; the rest took effect on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: The Constitution was brought into force on 26 January 1950 mainly because
o: the Objectives Resolution was adopted on 26 January 1947
the Cabinet Mission Plan was announced on 26 January 1946
26 January had been celebrated as Independence Day after the Purna Swaraj resolution of the Congress in 1930
questions.e: The Lahore session of the Congress (December 1929) adopted Purna Swaraj and 26 January 1930 was observed as Independence Day. The date was chosen to honour it.
questions.h: Purna Swaraj Day 1930 becomes Republic Day 1950.

questions.q:
Statement-I: After 15 August 1947 the Constituent Assembly functioned both as a constitution-making body and as the legislature of the Dominion.
Statement-II: The Indian Independence Act 1947 made the Constituent Assembly a fully sovereign body, free from British parliamentary control.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Once the Independence Act removed British control, the Assembly's authority extended to making ordinary laws too. In that role it was chaired by G.V. Mavalankar.

questions.q: The original handwritten (calligraphed) copy of the Constitution was illustrated by artists of Shantiniketan led by
questions.e: Nandalal Bose and his students painted scenes from India's history and culture, and the English text was calligraphed by Prem Behari Narain Raizada.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the framing of the Constitution:
1. The Constituent Assembly held 11 sessions in framing the Constitution.
2. 114 days were spent in considering the Draft Constitution.
3. The Constitution was passed after four readings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Constitution went through three readings, not four. The Assembly sat for 165 days over 11 sessions.

questions.q: The Constituent Assembly adopted the national flag on
questions.e: The Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag under Rajendra Prasad produced the tricolour, which was adopted before Independence on 22 July 1947.

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution came into force on 26 November 1949 rather than 26 January 1950?
questions.e: Provisions on citizenship (Articles 5 to 9), provisional Parliament, elections and temporary provisions needed to be effective at once to prepare for the first elections. The rest began on 26 January 1950.

questions.q:
Match the following features with the country from which they were borrowed:
A. Directive Principles of State Policy
B. Concurrent List
C. Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency
D. Residuary powers with the Centre

1. Canada
2. Ireland
3. Australia
4. Germany (Weimar Constitution)
Which one of the following is the correct matching?
questions.e: The residuary powers with the Centre come from Canada, the Concurrent List from Australia, DPSPs from Ireland and suspension of rights in an emergency from the Weimar Constitution.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Feature : Source
1. Fundamental Duties : Constitution of the USSR
2. Procedure for constitutional amendment : South Africa
3. Procedure established by law : Japan
4. Impeachment of the President : Ireland
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: Impeachment of the President is borrowed from the USA, not Ireland.

questions.q: The idea of nominating members to the Rajya Sabha was borrowed from the Constitution of
questions.e: Ireland also gave the method of election of the President and the Directive Principles. South Africa gave the amendment procedure and election of Rajya Sabha members.

questions.q:
Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution were taken from the Government of India Act 1935?
1. Federal scheme
2. Public Service Commissions
3. Concept of single citizenship
4. Office of Governor
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The federal scheme, Public Service Commissions and the office of Governor come from the 1935 Act. Single citizenship was borrowed from Britain.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature borrowed from the British Constitution?
questions.e: Britain gave the cabinet system, rule of law and single citizenship, while judicial review is taken from the American model.

questions.q: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from Canada?
o: Joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament
Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
questions.e: The Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction (Art 143) is from Canada. The Concurrent List and joint sitting are from Australia and Fundamental Duties from the USSR.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Poona Pact
2. Nehru Report
3. Appointment of the Simon Commission
4. Communal Award
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
questions.e: The Simon Commission (1927) was followed by the Nehru Report (1928) as India's reply, then the Communal Award (August 1932) and the Poona Pact (September 1932).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Federal Court of India:
1. It was established in 1937 under the Government of India Act 1935.
2. Sir Maurice Gwyer was its first Chief Justice.
3. The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on 26 January 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Supreme Court was inaugurated on 28 January 1950, two days after the Constitution came into force.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the demand for a Constituent Assembly:
1. M.N. Roy first proposed the idea in 1934.
2. The Indian National Congress made the official demand in 1935.
3. The British Government accepted the demand in principle in the August Offer of 1940.
4. The Wavell Plan of 1945 conceded the demand for a Constituent Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Wavell Plan dealt with the Executive Council, not a constituent body.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mountbatten Plan of 3 June 1947:
1. The legislative assemblies of Punjab and Bengal were to meet in two sections to decide on partition.
2. A referendum was to be held in the North-West Frontier Province and the Sylhet district of Assam.
3. A single Constituent Assembly was to frame the Constitution for both India and Pakistan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The plan led to separate Constituent Assemblies for India and Pakistan.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events of the Constituent Assembly in chronological order:
1. Constitution adopted
2. Objectives Resolution adopted
3. Drafting Committee set up
4. National flag adopted
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
questions.e: Objectives Resolution: 22 January 1947; flag: 22 July 1947; Drafting Committee: 29 August 1947; Constitution: 26 November 1949.
